mbm-1526.clue: My computer keeps a very small garden.
mbm-1526.quote: I wrote a watering game for Mum. If she forgets it for a week the plants turn into cacti. She says it's the first house she's owned where the ferns understand her.

mbm-1527.clue: Watch the eyebrows when I change hands.
mbm-1527.quote: My glove puppet plays both grandfathers in our street play. One fuzzy eyebrow sticks up, the other hangs down. I can hear the children calling the next grandpa before I even change my voice.

mbm-1528.clue: I keep a thimble for a drummer I've never met.
mbm-1528.quote: My smallest puppet has a thimble for a drum. The front row can never hear it, so my sister in the wings taps her teacup at exactly the right moment.

mbm-1529.clue: I gave the weakest card its own velvet sleeve.
mbm-1529.quote: The little mushroom guard has never won a fight. My niece drew his portrait in wax crayon, so now he's the first card I play. He's getting awfully good at losing in style.

mbm-1530.clue: The one with the crescent is mine.
mbm-1530.quote: I pinch a little moon into my arepa before it hits the griddle. Last Sunday my whole family made moons. I bit into five different fillings before I found my cheese.

mbm-1531.clue: I've got a photograph of the back of a clock.
mbm-1531.quote: All our guidebooks showed the clock tower from the square. A caretaker took me behind the face. Now when people show me the famous clock I think of his red lunchbox beside the gears.

mbm-1532.clue: I put the sea exactly where the stain was.
mbm-1532.quote: I spilled blue ink on a half-finished quilt. My neighbor handed me a green scrap and asked where the coast went. Now there's an island there with a lighthouse that used to be a sleeve.

mbm-1533.clue: My shirt button has a spare passenger.
mbm-1533.quote: I sew a little red loop beneath every top button. Dad can hang his reading glasses there when he takes them off. He still pats his head first.

mbm-1534.clue: We settle disagreements with three little bowls.
mbm-1534.quote: My sisters couldn't agree on an arepa filling, so I made a tasting plate with three miniature breads. Mum ate the lot and declared the judge needed another round.

mbm-1535.clue: I saved half a dance on a paper napkin.
mbm-1535.quote: Our bus arrived halfway through a foxtrot. My partner marked where our shoes had been with two sugar cubes on the café napkin. We picked it up on Sunday.

mbm-1536.clue: I like a teapot with a good singing voice.
mbm-1536.quote: The first time I filled my pot, the lid whistled. I spent a week throwing lids that fit better. The family still insists I bring the noisy one to tea.

mbm-1537.clue: My ticket gets folded into four little feet.
mbm-1537.quote: The cinema lady used to fold every torn ticket into a paper dog for me. I saw her at a matinee last month and folded one for her. She tucked it behind the glass.

mbm-1538.clue: I keep a flashlight in my coat for the walk home.
mbm-1538.quote: After the last song our shadows walked halfway up the wall outside the club. We played the chorus again by flashlight and made the shadows take the encore.

mbm-1539.clue: My shortest scarf is worn by the tallest thing in the room.
mbm-1539.quote: The first scarf I crocheted came out the length of a ruler. I tied it round the neck of Dad's double bass. He wears a plain tie to gigs so the bass can be the flashy one.

mbm-1540.clue: I set aside the controller with the squeak.
mbm-1540.quote: My best friend plays the platform level with his eyes shut while I call the jumps. The squeaky button lets me hear when he's ready. We finally got across that purple bridge together.

mbm-1541.clue: Hold my little flag up to the sun.
mbm-1541.quote: I cut our old family bicycle into tissue for the courtyard. When the wind blows through the paper, the spokes throw a wheel of shadows onto the breakfast table.

mbm-1542.clue: I take the longest way to the last page.
mbm-1542.quote: There's a chapter where the old ferryman comes home. I read it on the actual ferry every year. The boatman knows to squeeze my shoulder when it's time to get off.

mbm-1543.clue: My grandmother shuffles with a dish towel.
mbm-1543.quote: The baby started sleeping through domino night when Gran put a folded towel under the tiles. We learned to slam doubles quietly. You should see what our faces do instead.

mbm-1544.clue: I left one coin taped to the cabinet.
mbm-1544.quote: Our arcade was closing. I taped a coin under the joystick so the next owner could have the first turn. Years later I found that machine in a bowling alley. The coin was gone.

mbm-1545.clue: I wash the paddle before I wash my shoes.
mbm-1545.quote: I let my niece paint blue waves on one blade. Every time it rose from the river she'd call out that the water was coming with us. I leave the chipped paint where it is.

mbm-1546.clue: Look for the square that puckers in the middle.
mbm-1546.quote: I stitched a drawstring pouch inside our picnic quilt. That's where the napkins go. My cousin used it to hide the last biscuit, so now we pack an extra one.

mbm-1547.clue: I give my props a dress rehearsal in the fruit bowl.
mbm-1547.quote: I painted a wooden juggling apple so well my brother tried to bite it. His little tooth marks tell me where it will wobble. That's my most reliable apple now.

mbm-1548.clue: I can spot my ball in the dark.
mbm-1548.quote: My first bowling ball has a milky streak that looks like a comet. Under the alley's black light the tail glows before the pins do. I wait for it every time.

mbm-1549.clue: The crooked print is the one I framed.
mbm-1549.quote: I took twelve careful portraits of my uncle and one by accident when he tripped over the cable release. That's the one where you can see exactly how he laughs.

mbm-1550.clue: I pack the smallest plate first.
mbm-1550.quote: When my sister started lifting, every plate at the club looked enormous. I painted a ladybird on the smallest one. Now she looks for it before she even takes off her coat.
